claims.head: Watch the Rangers’ puck management
claims.call: The Devils get at least their usual 7.8% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
claims.body: The Devils turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Rangers are around the middle of the league at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Rangers.
claims.nums: New Jersey 3rd for chances off turnovers (7.8% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · NY Rangers 22nd for avoiding breakdowns
claims.gist: The Devils pounce on loose pucks, and the Rangers cough them up.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 6 games this season

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 expected goals within 5 seconds of winning the puck
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Rangers hit; the Devils mostly don’t
claims.body: On physicality, the Rangers is one of the league’s best and New Jersey is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.gist: The Rangers and the Devils sit at opposite ends for physicality.
claims.call: The Rangers hit more than the Devils in the close stretches of the game.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 6 and 4 games this season

check.measure: hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average)
check.rule: held if the team comes out ahead by at least half its usual margin; partly if it comes out ahead by less; otherwise didn't happen

notes.text: S. Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 44% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 7% last season.

NJD.head: The matchup suits New Jersey
NJD.body: New Jersey has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. The Rangers can make it interesting if they pounce on loose pucks.
